transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I’m here because things have been happening for months now, and people keep telling me it’s just little mistakes, but it’s not. My sister’s appointments get moved around, bills come in wrong, people say they’ll call me back and then they “forget”—and I know how offices work, I supervised that kind of thing for years, so I can tell when something is being handled normally and when it isn’t.

It’s like information is being kept from me. Everyone acts like I’m overreacting, but there’s a pattern. And I feel like they’re trying to push me out of decisions I should be part of. I mean, even the way messages get passed along—well, not passed along, that’s the point. It’s just… I came in because I need someone to understand that this isn’t just random.
Do you think someone is intentionally doing these things to you?

Yes… I mean, I don’t think all of it is accidental. Not after this many months. My sister’s appointments get shifted, then a bill comes in wrong, then someone says they were supposed to call me back but “forgot”—and people say, oh, offices make mistakes, but I worked in offices for years, I supervised people, I know the difference between a mistake and a pattern.

It feels like information is being kept from me, like they’re trying to edge me out of decisions I’m supposed to be part of. And, you know, my sister doesn’t always notice these things the way I do—she’ll just say, “let it go,” but that’s how people get taken advantage of. So yes, I think someone is doing it on purpose, or at least letting it happen on purpose.
Do you think these people are targeting you specifically?

Yes, I do. Maybe it started with my sister’s stuff, her appointments being moved around and the bills being wrong, but I’m the one who catches it, so then I’m the problem to them. That’s how it feels.

And I worked in offices, I know how messages are supposed to be handled. You don’t just “forget” over and over unless someone is keeping things from you or trying to make you look difficult. My sister says I should just let it go, but that’s easy to say when you’re not the one being pushed out of decisions.
Do you think these events are somehow related to you or your life in a special way, beyond just being targeted?

I don’t know if I’d say “special,” exactly… but it is related to me, because I’m the one who notices. I’m the one asking questions and keeping track. For months it’s been the same kind of thing—my sister’s appointments moved, bills wrong, people saying they forgot to call me back—and everyone acts like these are separate little mistakes.

But they’re not separate. When you’ve worked in offices like I have, you know how things are supposed to go. I used to supervise people doing this kind of work, and you learn very quickly when something is just sloppy and when information is being held back. And somehow it always ends with me being pushed out of decisions I should be part of. So yes, it feels connected to me in that way.
Do you think these people who are supposedly doing these things to you are plotting against you in a coordinated way?

Coordinated… I don’t know if they’re all sitting in a room making a plan, if that’s what you mean. But it feels connected. For months now it’s the same pattern—my sister’s appointments get moved, then the bills are wrong, then someone “forgets” to call me back. And somehow I’m always the one left without the information.

I worked in offices a long time, you know, and when you supervise people you learn how things are supposed to flow—messages, records, callbacks, all of that. My old manager used to say, “One mistake is a mistake, three mistakes is a system,” and that’s sort of what I keep thinking about. Everyone tells me it’s just errors, but I know when information is being kept from me. It’s like they’re trying to push me out of decisions I’m supposed to be part of.
Do you believe that these events are happening because of something specific about you, such as your thoughts or actions?

I don’t think it’s my thoughts, like I’m making it happen by thinking something. But my actions, maybe—because I keep asking questions. I keep noticing when things don’t add up.

That’s why I’m here, really. For months it’s been the same pattern: my sister’s appointments get moved, bills come wrong, people say they “forgot” to call me back. And everyone says, oh, it’s just mistakes, but I worked in offices, I know how records and calls are supposed to be handled. If you keep pressing, some people don’t like that.

It reminds me of when I was supervising staff and someone would “misplace” paperwork after being corrected—anyway, that’s what I mean. It feels like because I’m the one keeping track, they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.
Do you think it's possible that there could be another explanation for these events, other than someone intentionally trying to keep information from you?

I mean… I suppose anything is possible, sure. People do make mistakes. I’ve made mistakes in offices myself—once we had a whole stack of invoices filed under the wrong vendor because someone changed the label and nobody told the rest of us, and then everyone blamed the front desk.

But this is why I’m here, because it’s not just one thing. For months now it’s been the same pattern with my sister’s appointments getting moved, bills showing up wrong, people saying they “forgot” to call me back. And everyone keeps telling me it’s just mistakes, but I know what it looks like when information is being kept from someone. It feels like they’re trying to push me out of decisions I should be part of.
Do you think it's possible that you might be mistaken about someone intentionally keeping information from you?

I hear what you’re asking… could I be mistaken. I mean, in a general sense, yes, people can be wrong. I know that. I supervised office staff for years, and half the job was sorting out misunderstandings—someone puts a note in the wrong folder, someone assumes someone else made the call, that kind of thing.

But this doesn’t feel like that. I’m here because for months now I keep seeing the same pattern: my sister’s appointments get moved, the bills show up wrong, people “forget” to call me back, and then I’m the one who doesn’t have the information. And everyone keeps saying it’s just mistakes, but I know what it looks like when information is being kept from someone. It feels like they’re trying to push me out of decisions I should be part of.
Do you think these beliefs about people keeping information from you could be considered unreasonable by others?

I’m sure they would call it unreasonable. My sister already gives me that look, like I’m making too much of it. But I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern—appointments get moved, bills come in wrong, people say they “forgot” to call me back.

And, you know, I worked in offices, so I notice these things. There’s a way information flows when people want you included, and there’s a way it suddenly gets messy when they don’t. So maybe other people think I’m overreacting, but to me it’s pretty clear they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.
Do you think it's possible that you could change your mind about people keeping information from you if you found out more information?

I mean… if there were real information, yes, I would look at it. I’m not someone who refuses paperwork or facts—honestly, in my old office, I was usually the one telling people to check the forms before jumping to conclusions. We had this one woman who would swear the copier was “eating” her reports, and it turned out she was saving them to the wrong folder every time.

But this is different. I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern with my sister—appointments moved around, bills showing up wrong, people saying they “forgot” to call me back. And somehow I’m always the last to know. Everyone says it’s just mistakes, but after a while it stops looking like mistakes. It feels like they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions. So… I guess if I found out more, maybe, but it would have to explain all of that, not just one little piece.
Would you say that your belief about people keeping information from you is something that you are completely certain about, or is it something that you could potentially change your mind about?

Completely certain is a strong phrase… I mean, I suppose anyone could change their mind if someone actually showed them something that made sense. I’m not trying to be stubborn for the sake of it.

But I’ve been around offices long enough to know when things are just normal confusion and when they keep happening in the same direction. With my sister, it’s been months of this—appointments getting moved, bills showing up wrong, people saying they “forgot” to call me back. And somehow I’m the one left out, every time.

So could I change my mind? Maybe, if there were a real explanation. But right now, no, I feel pretty certain. It really seems like information is being kept from me, like they’re trying to push me out of decisions I should be part of.
How much time do you spend each day thinking about the possibility that people are keeping information from you?

It’s hard to put an exact number on it. I don’t sit down with a timer or anything, but it comes up a lot during the day—especially when I’m waiting for a call back or a bill doesn’t look right, or my sister tells me something after the fact.

I’ll try to go do something else, and then I’ll think, well, why didn’t they tell me that sooner? At work, you know, if one person was always left off the email chain, that usually meant something. So I can’t just brush it off.

I’d say… several hours altogether, probably. Not all at once, but on and off. Because for months now it’s been the same pattern—appointments moved, bills wrong, people “forgetting” to call—and everyone says mistakes, but it feels too consistent. It feels like they’re keeping information from me and pushing me out of decisions.
Do you think the people keeping information from you are doing it for a reason that doesn't make sense to most people?

I don’t know if it “doesn’t make sense” to most people. I think if they saw the whole thing laid out, maybe it would make more sense. Like, in an office, if one person keeps getting left off meeting notes, and then their paperwork is always late, and then people say, “Oh, sorry, I forgot”—after a while you stop calling that random.

With my sister, it’s been the same kind of thing for months. Her appointments get moved, bills come in wrong, people don’t call me back, and then everyone acts like I’m overreacting. But I know they’re keeping information from me. I think they’re trying to push me out of decisions.

Now, whether other people understand the reason… I don’t know. People don’t always understand office politics either until they’re the one being cut out.
Do you find it difficult to focus on other things because you're thinking about people keeping information from you?

Yes, sometimes. I mean, I still get things done—I’m not sitting there unable to function—but it does pull my attention away.

Like at work, if someone makes a routine mistake, something I probably would’ve just corrected before, I find myself pushing harder now. Asking why it happened, who told them what, whether anyone else knew. And then the conversation gets uncomfortable, because people look at me like I’m making more of it than I should. But in an office, details matter. I’ve supervised people long enough to know that.

And with family meetings about my sister, it’s gotten tense. I’ll try to listen, but then I’m watching for what isn’t being said, or why I’m only hearing something at the last minute. So yes, it affects my focus some. I’m still managing my responsibilities, but people are definitely reacting differently to me now.
Are you having trouble enjoying activities you used to like because of these thoughts about people keeping information from you?

I guess… yes, in a way. I still do things, I’m not just sitting around staring at the wall or anything. But it’s harder to enjoy them when part of my mind is going back over who said what, or why I heard something late.

And it spills over. Family meetings have become tense, because I’m listening for what’s being left out, and at work I’ve had a few uncomfortable conversations because I’ve pressed people harder about routine mistakes than I used to. I used to be able to let some things go, you know, depending on the situation.

So I’m still managing my responsibilities. I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t function. But it has started to affect how people respond to me, and that makes it harder to relax and enjoy things.
Do you find yourself thinking about people keeping information from you more often than you think about other things in your daily life?

Yes… probably more than I should, if I’m being honest. It comes up a lot during the day because it’s not just one thing. For months now it’s been the same pattern with my sister—appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people say they “forgot” to call me back.

And I know people will say, well, offices make mistakes, billing departments are a mess—believe me, I’ve worked around paperwork long enough to know that. I had one clerk years ago who could misfile a form three different ways before lunch. But this isn’t like that. This feels like information is being kept from me, like I’m being pushed out of decisions.

So yes, I do think about it a lot. Even when I’m trying to focus on something else, part of me is still putting the pieces together.
Do you think there's any evidence that could change your mind about people keeping information from you?

I don’t know what evidence would change my mind, honestly. I mean, if this had happened once or twice, sure, I’d say maybe it was a mistake. Offices make mistakes, bills get entered wrong, people forget calls—I’ve supervised clerical work long enough to know that happens.

But this has been going on for months with my sister. Appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people say they “forgot” to call me back, and somehow I’m always finding out late. After a while it stops looking accidental. It feels like the same pattern over and over, like I’m being kept out of decisions.

Maybe if everyone sat down and showed me everything clearly, ahead of time, without things missing… maybe. But even then, I’d wonder why it took that much pushing to get it. So no, not easily. I think they are keeping information from me.
Have your thoughts about people keeping information from you caused problems in your relationships with family or friends?

Yes, it has. Mostly with family… those meetings get tense now. I’m listening so closely for what’s not being said that I know I probably come across sharp, but if people would just be straightforward, it wouldn’t turn into that.

And, I mean, it reminds me of work too—because in an office, when one small thing gets entered wrong, it can turn into three different problems by Friday. I’ve seen that for years. But lately I’ve been pressing people harder over routine mistakes than I used to, and a few conversations have gotten uncomfortable because of it.

I’m still doing what I need to do. I don’t want anyone thinking I’ve fallen apart. But yes, it’s affected how people respond to me, and that’s made things strained.
Do you think your beliefs about people keeping information from you might be an exaggeration of real issues or misunderstandings?

I can see how someone might call it an exaggeration, yes, because each thing by itself could be explained away. An appointment gets moved, a bill is wrong, somebody forgets to call back—when I worked in an office, that kind of thing happened all the time. We had filing systems that looked organized until one person put something in the wrong folder, and then everyone acted like nobody knew who touched it.

But this isn’t just one mix-up. For months now, it’s been the same pattern with my sister. Things change, I find out late, and then everyone says, “Oh, it was just a mistake.” After a while, that starts to feel very convenient.

So… no, I don’t really think it’s only a misunderstanding. Maybe some of the small pieces are mistakes, but overall I know information is being kept from me. It feels like I’m being pushed out of decisions, and I don’t think I’m imagining that.
Do you think you could ever stop believing that people are keeping information from you?

I don’t know. “Ever” is a big word.

I mean, I’m not trying to be stubborn just to be stubborn. If things were handled openly, if I was told ahead of time and the bills matched what actually happened and people returned calls when they said they would… maybe I could relax some. But that’s not what’s been happening.

For months now it’s been the same thing with my sister—appointments moved, bills wrong, people “forgetting” to call me back—and then everybody acts like I’m making too much of it. I worked in offices, I know mistakes happen, but when the same kind of mistake keeps leaving me out, it doesn’t feel like a mistake anymore.

So could I stop believing it? Not while it keeps happening. I know they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.
